_about: Retrieval eval for the recipe corpus. Relevance is by DOCUMENT ID (a doc's recipe_name), not by keyword substring: the old proxy counted a chunk relevant if it contained a word like 'chicken', which structurally favoured BM25 and hit a ceiling because common words appear in a large fraction of 3,090 documents. Each query here is phrased to describe a dish WITHOUT using words from its title, so a retriever cannot win by lexical overlap alone.
_caveat: Starter set built by the assistant, validated so every gold ID exists in the corpus. It is NOT a domain-reviewed gold standard: relevance judgments are one person's opinion of what a query should return, and other recipes in the corpus may be equally relevant but unlabelled, which depresses recall. Treat absolute numbers with suspicion; treat A/B differences between retrieval configs, read together with the bootstrap CI, as the signal.

_fields.query: the user query sent to the retriever
_fields.expects: legacy keyword proxy, used only when relevant_ids is absent
_fields.match_all: legacy; require ALL keyword terms (default false)
